headline: One-time gain lifts EPS, underlying growth stays modest

kpis.label: FFO per share (available for common stockholders)

summary_short: Highwoods posted Q2 FY2026 diluted EPS of $0.85 (+400% y/y), driven mostly by a $79.0M gain on property disposition versus none a year ago, while rental and other revenue rose 7.9% y/y to $216.4M on acquisitions and a 1.4% same-property NOI gain.
summary_long: Rental and other revenue rose 7.9% y/y to $216.4M on acquisitions in Raleigh, Charlotte and Dallas plus 1.4% same-property NOI growth, partly offset by dispositions. Diluted EPS jumped to $0.85 from $0.17 y/y, but that swing is almost entirely a $79.0M Q2 gain on property disposition versus $0 a year ago, not operating improvement. FFO per share rose modestly to $0.90 from $0.89 y/y. Occupancy improved to 85.7% from 85.3% at year-end 2025; management guides occupancy to 86.0%-87.0% for the remainder of 2026. New/renewal leases signed in Q2 carried GAAP rents 20.9% above expiring leases. Cash stood at $145.4M with the full $749.9M revolver undrawn; quarterly dividend held at $0.50/share, declared again for Q3 on July 22.

drivers.explanation: Company attributes the quarter to property acquisitions in Raleigh, Charlotte and Dallas, higher same-property NOI, and Raleigh development completions, partially offset by property dispositions and higher interest expense.
Acquisitions added $15.6M, same-property revenue added $5.4M, and completed Raleigh developments added $1.2M, partly offset by a $6.4M decrease from dispositions.
The $0.68 y/y EPS increase is driven almost entirely by a $79.0M gain on disposition of property in Q2 2026 versus none in Q2 2025 — a one-time item, not core operating growth.
Same-property NOI rose $1.8M (1.4%) as a $5.4M increase in same-property revenue outpaced a $3.7M rise in same-property operating expenses (utilities, repairs/maintenance, contract services).
not explained in the release beyond general leasing/vacancy mechanics; no acquisition- or building-specific cause is cited for the 40bp move.
Board declared the same $0.50/share dividend paid in Q1 2026 and Q2 2025, and declared it again on July 22, 2026 for the Q3 payment.
